$comment: The lists under Settings → Tracking: accounts, categories, tags, debts, recurring (settings/accounts.tsx, categories.tsx, tags.tsx, debts.tsx, recurring.tsx).

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.intro: An account is somewhere money sits: cash, a card, a bank account. Every transaction belongs to one, balances and net worth are added up from them, and a group (“Personal”, “Business”) is how the app is scoped to a subset of them.
accounts.emptyHint: Tap + to add one, or restore a backup in Settings.

group.note: Section header for accounts that are in no group.

current.note: Row subtitle of the account the app treats as current; type is "Card".

archivedType.note: Row subtitle of an archived account; type is "Card".

categories.title: Categories
categories.intro: A category is what money was spent on, and it is what budgets and every chart are built from. A folder groups categories and is never filed into: a transaction always goes to one of the categories inside it. Give a folder a colour and the categories created in it take that colour.
categories.mattersNone: Not set yet · two questions, five minutes

mattersPartial.note: How many categories have an importance set, and how many do not.

categories.emptyHint: Add a folder, then categories inside it.

folder.message: Folder · {count, plural, one {# category} other {# categories}}

folderIncome.message: Folder · income · {count, plural, one {# category} other {# categories}}
folderIncome.note: Subtitle of a folder that holds income.

categories.archivedNote: Everything already filed under these keeps its category and still counts in budgets and charts; they are simply not offered when anything new is filed. Open one to bring it back.

tags.title: Tags
tags.intro: A tag cuts across categories, where a category says what the money was for: #work lunch, #vacation fuel. A tag can be limited to the categories it makes sense in, a budget can be set on one, and travel mode tags a whole journey for you.

uses.note: How many transactions carry the tag.

usesOnly.message: {count, plural, one {# use} other {# uses}} · only for {categories}
usesOnly.note: categories is a comma-separated list of category names.

tags.usesAny: {count, plural, one {# use} other {# uses}} · any category
tags.usesArchived: {count, plural, one {# use} other {# uses}} · archived

travel.note: Section header: tags made by travel mode, one per trip.

tags.archivedNote: Transactions keep these tags and budgets on them still count; they are just not offered for anything new. Open one to bring it back.

debts.title: Debts
debts.intro: Money lent to someone, or borrowed from them. A debt is not a transaction and touches no balance — it becomes one only when it is actually paid, which settling it here writes for you. Give it a due date and a reminder fires the day before and on the day, at a time you choose.

recurring.title: Recurring

fallbackTitle.note: Name of a rule with no payee and no category.

noRate.message: No rate yet for {currencies} — those rules are not counted.

recurring.waitSubtitle: Let the real payment arrive and settle the rule, instead of adding one on the day

days.note: How long a rule waits for the bank's charge.

recurring.noteWait: A rule for money that comes back: rent, subscriptions, salary. With waiting on, a rule keeps quiet on its day: the payment your bank notifies — or one you log yourself — is taken as that month’s, with the rule’s category and the amount actually charged. Only if nothing turns up within the window does the rule act: automatic ones post their own amount, manual ones ask. Individual rules can wait longer or less. Kopiyka also spots repeats in what you have already logged and offers them below.
recurring.noteNoWait: A rule for money that comes back: rent, subscriptions, salary. An automatic rule posts itself on the day and tells you it did; a manual one waits and asks first, for a payment whose day or amount moves around. If the Shortcut automation already logs these payments, turn on waiting above so they are not added twice. Kopiyka also spots repeats in what you have already logged and offers them below.

suggestionPlanned.note: A rule suggested from a future-dated entry (a payment logged ahead of its day). freq is "monthly", date "22 Sep".

suggestionSeen.note: A rule suggested from repeats in history; count is how many times it was seen.

expectedPosts.message: Expected {date} · posts if nothing arrives within {days}
expectedPosts.note: date is "22 Sep"; days is "3 days".

expectedAsks.message: Expected {date} · asks if nothing arrives within {days}
expectedAsks.note: date is "22 Sep"; days is "3 days".

recurring.footWait: Totals cover active rules only, every cadence normalised to a year. Reminders are local notifications on this phone; a rule acts only once its window has closed without a charge.
recurring.footNoWait: Totals cover active rules only, every cadence normalised to a year. Reminders are local notifications on this phone; automatic rules post on the day, manual ones wait for your tap.

posting.title: How does it get paid?
posting.autoSubtitle: It leaves your account by itself — a subscription or standing order on a fixed day. Kopiyka adds it for you and tells you it did.
posting.manualSubtitle: The day or the amount moves around, so Kopiyka asks first and you post it once it has actually gone out.

source.title: Where does it come from?
source.txSubtitle: Pick one you already logged — title, amount, category, tags and how often are filled in
source.newSubtitle: Amount and name, then the rest on the rule screen

recurring.name: What is it called?

daily.note: How often a rule repeats; count is the interval.
